verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Stabilizing Above the Capitulation Low, but No Catalyst Before CPI
verdict.rationale_short: After Saturday's ~$59,227 capitulation, BTC steadied back toward ~$60,500 and ETH held near ~$1,710 on a quieter Sunday — the forced-selling cascade has paused, but nothing has changed the cause. The macro that broke the trade (a 30Y above 5.0%, a firm dollar, delayed Fed cuts, an active Iran conflict) is unresolved, Strategy's selling and ETF outflows remain an overhang, and total market cap is still ~48% off its peak. The verdict steps back up from bearish to STEP ASIDE: the immediate liquidation risk has eased, but with May CPI on June 10 the next real catalyst and equities reopening Monday into the same hostile regime, this is a stabilization to watch, not to buy. The first constructive triggers are an ETH reclaim of ~$1,674 and a BTC reclaim of $66,000 on falling VIX.

bear_case: A weekend stabilization above the capitulation low is the most seductive trap in a bear market — it invites dip-buyers right before the catalyst that decides direction. Nothing that caused the ~48% drawdown has changed: the 30Y is above 5.0%, the dollar is firm, the Iran conflict is live, and Strategy's selling and ETF outflows remain an overhang. Monday reopens equities into the same broken regime, and CPI lands Wednesday. Invalidation: a daily close below $59,000 BTC confirms the next leg toward $52-55K; only an ETH reclaim of $1,674 and a BTC reclaim of $66,000 on falling VIX — ideally after a cool CPI — signal the low is in.
